title: Google Analytics vs Fathom
description: Google Analytics 4 vs Fathom Analytics — compare free Google ecosystem analytics vs privacy-first hosted web analytics.
verdict: Choose Fathom when you want a polished, privacy-oriented traffic dashboard without GA4 complexity or cookie-heavy tracking. Choose GA4 when Google Ads, Search Console, BigQuery, or free scale matter more than simplicity and privacy posture.
quickAnswer: **Fathom** is the better fit if privacy, dashboard clarity, and a lightweight marketing report matter most. **Google Analytics 4** is the better fit if you need free deep analytics tied to Google’s advertising and data ecosystem.
bottomLine: Fathom wins the "I want analytics someone will actually open" contest for many marketing sites. GA4 wins when paid search, app+web, or warehouse export are non-negotiable. Hosted Fathom starts around $15/month for 100K pageviews; GA4 standard remains $0 with higher compliance and learning costs.

faq.question: Is Fathom a GA4 replacement?
faq.answer: For many blogs and marketing sites, yes — if you mainly need pages, referrers, UTMs, and goals. It does not replace Google Ads attribution, BigQuery export, or GA4’s exploratory depth.

faq.question: Does Fathom need a cookie banner?
faq.answer: Fathom is designed as privacy-first and cookie-light. Many teams run it without a banner in some EU contexts, but you should still verify with legal counsel for your jurisdiction and configuration.

faq.question: Is Google Analytics free compared to Fathom?
faq.answer: GA4 standard is free. Fathom bills on pageview tiers (entry around $15/month for 100K pageviews). Factor consent tooling and analyst time into GA4’s true cost.

faq.question: Can I self-host Fathom?
faq.answer: Hosted Fathom Analytics is cloud-only. Fathom Lite is a separate free self-hosted product with fewer features and no vendor support. For open-source self-hosting with an active community, also compare Plausible and Umami.

faq.question: Which script is lighter?
faq.answer: On our recorded Slow-4G fixture, Fathom transferred about 2.7 KiB with roughly +251 ms load overhead. GA4 transferred about 171 KiB with roughly +1.16 s overhead. See the benchmarks hub for full details.

editorialNotes.title: Privacy vs ecosystem
editorialNotes.content: This is the classic GA escape tradeoff. Fathom trades Google’s free depth for a readable, privacy-oriented SaaS. If your growth engine is Google Ads, staying on GA4 (or running both) is usually safer than a hard cutover.

editorialNotes.title: Performance
editorialNotes.content: We publish recorded script benchmarks for both tools. Color bands on those pages use absolute thresholds documented on [methodology](/methodology/).
